text: Roots −1 and 0; getFail; counts through fail links.

The palindromic tree (回文树 , palindromic automaton, PAM) stores every distinct palindrome of a string as a node: at most n + 2 nodes. Two roots: length −1 (so that adding a character c on both sides gives a length-1 palindrome) and length 0. Edge c from node v leads to cvc. fail[v] = the longest proper palindromic suffix of v.

Add characters one by one. Keep last = the longest palindromic suffix of the current prefix. To extend with s[i], follow fail links from last until s[i − len − 1] == s[i]; then the new node is c + that + c. Its fail link is found the same way, starting from the old node's fail. Amortised O(n).

Line 1: how many palindromes end at each position (num[v] = depth along fail links, the P5496 quantity). Line 2: number of distinct palindromes (tot − 1, the two roots excluded). Line 3: the largest occurrences × length (P3649 回文串). All three are checked by brute force in Python.

fail of a new length-1 palindrome must be node 0 (empty), not node 1; ch[...] returns 0 when missing, which is exactly that. Index checks i − len − 1 ≥ 0 are needed because the string has no sentinel. Counting occurrences needs nodes processed from longer to shorter; creation order already is.

Compare with Manacher (第3章): Manacher gives the longest palindrome at each centre; PAM gives the set of distinct palindromes with counts and suffix links, which DP on palindromes needs (双倍回文 P4287: a palindrome whose half is also a palindrome, found by walking fail links).
